title: Form and Input Selectors
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of form and input selectors in a jQuery application.
Apply input elements by type in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify text and password inputs with an explicit test or browser observation.
status_note: Draft generated from the attached syllabus and official references; requires lesson-by-lesson technical review, local execution, accessibility checks, and editorial approval.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through form and input selectors with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns input elements by type into a repeatable implementation choice. Selectors describe which DOM elements to match; use standard CSS selectors first, then filter or test a collection when that makes intent clearer.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Selectors describe which DOM elements to match; use standard CSS selectors first, then filter or test a collection when that makes intent clearer.

content_blocks.expected_output: Counts enabled input controls. Prefer standard CSS selectors where they express the same condition clearly.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a local HTML page with jQuery 4.0.0 loaded before app.js for JavaScript snippets. HTML and package-manager snippets can be checked as configuration examples. Run the interaction in browser DevTools, inspect the DOM/Network panel, and compare actual behavior with the expected result. Do not submit learner code to the production API for arbitrary execution.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original markup and code, clear console/network filters, reload the local page, and repeat the same interaction. For a request example, return the mock endpoint to its original response before retrying.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a known DOM structure, apply the pattern for form and input selectors, and test one normal case plus one edge case. Keep selectors scoped to the intended component and verify the real browser result.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create markup with at least three matching and non-matching elements, then implement form and input selectors and verify which elements are selected.

task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates form and input selectors using a current, documented approach.
The learner records the expected and actual behavior and checks at least one edge case.
The example preserves semantic HTML and does not render untrusted data as HTML.
The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.
hints: First identify which DOM nodes and runtime state are involved in form and input selectors.
Make one small change, inspect the resulting element or request, and compare it with the expected result.
If the result differs, check the selector, script order, browser console, event target, and relevant API documentation before adding more code.
content.expected_output: Counts enabled input controls. Prefer standard CSS selectors where they express the same condition clearly.
common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
